svg.title: Identify the color space linearly with the Lie algebra, writing C(a) for that identification. The map (a, n) 7→exp(C(a)) exp n has invertible derivative C(a) + n at zero. Its local smooth ambient inverse defines the color component logG. For a nearby group element its normal component van- ishes by the preceding isolation. Thus logG(exp(C(a))) = a for small a. Conversely, if g has inverse coordinates (a, n), then exp n = exp(−C(a))g ∈G with n small, so n = 0 and exp(C(logG g)) = g. Shrinking the color ball gives an open exponential image in G, since the continuous inverse sends a group neighborhood of each image point back into the ball. This requires neither connectedness of G nor a global logarithm. Define Fu(a) = logG(u exp(C(a))) on its chart domain, A(a) = DFexp(−C(a))(a) and J(a) = det A(a). Smoothness and the identity germ give J(0) = 1. If b = Fu(a), the germ identity Fexp(−C(a)) = Fexp(−C(b)) ◦Fu yields
